28070: Smooth, flattering and aggrieved; presents himself as the champion of the overlooked while nursing resentment.
28088: Wisdom and understanding given by God

28093: When Adonijah claims the throne, David orders Solomon anointed by Zadok and Nathan at the Gihon spring.
28095: He has Adonijah, Joab and Shimei executed and banishes Abiathar; 'the kingdom was established in the hand of Solomon'.
28097: In a dream God offers him anything; he asks for an understanding heart to govern, and is promised riches and honour too.
28099: He orders a disputed baby cut in two and identifies the true mother by her compassion.

28106: Visit of the queen of Sheba

28112:
Solomon, son of David and Bathsheba, ruled Israel at the height of its power and wealth. Asking God for wisdom rather than riches, he became proverbial for it, and he built the temple in Jerusalem that became the centre of Israel's worship for nearly four hundred years. His prayer at its dedication is one of the great prayers of the Old Testament.

His reign also had a darker side that the text does not hide. He secured the throne through executions, laid heavy forced labour and taxation on the northern tribes, multiplied horses, silver and wives against the warnings of Deut 17:16-17, and in old age built shrines for the gods of his foreign wives. God's verdict is that the kingdom will be divided after him, which happens at once under his son Rehoboam.

Tradition links Solomon with Proverbs, Ecclesiastes and the Song of Songs, and Jesus refers to his glory and his wisdom as benchmarks that the kingdom of God surpasses.
28113: Son of David and Bathsheba (2 Sam 12:24), anointed king (1 Kgs 1:39), asked for wisdom (1 Kgs 3:9), built the temple and palace (1 Kgs 6-7), wrote 3,000 proverbs and 1,005 songs (1 Kgs 4:32), loved many foreign women who turned his heart (1 Kgs 11:1-4), reigned forty years (1 Kgs 11:42). Headings attribute parts of Proverbs (Prov 1:1; 10:1; 25:1), the Song (Song 1:1) and Pss 72 and 127 to him; Ecclesiastes speaks as 'son of David, king in Jerusalem' (Eccl 1:1). Jesus says one greater than Solomon is here (Matt 12:42).
28114: Solomon is the wise king and temple builder; rabbinic tradition attributes the Song, Proverbs and Ecclesiastes to him at different stages of life, while critiquing his marriages. Later legends make him master of demons and speaker with animals.
28115: Solomon is read as a type of Christ the wise king and temple builder; the Wisdom of Solomon (deuterocanonical) is associated with his name. Patristic writers disputed whether he finally repented, some reading Ecclesiastes as a confession of old age.
28116: Emphasis falls on the danger of a divided heart: a king blessed with wisdom who failed to obey. Many evangelicals hold Solomonic authorship of most of Proverbs and of Ecclesiastes and Song; others accept that Ecclesiastes uses a Solomonic persona.
28117: Scholars debate the scale of Solomon's kingdom. Some attribute the six-chambered gates at Hazor, Megiddo and Gezer to Solomon (Yadin, Mazar); the low chronology (Finkelstein) dates them to the 9th-century Omrides. No contemporary inscription names Solomon. Most critical scholars date Ecclesiastes to the Persian or Hellenistic period.
28120: Temple building and dedicatory prayer (1 Kgs 8)
28123: Accumulating horses, gold and wives (1 Kgs 10:26-11:3; Deut 17:16-17)
28124: Building shrines to Chemosh and Molech (1 Kgs 11:7-8)
28126: Temple dedication and second appearance of God (1 Kgs 9:1-9)
28128: Solomon's reign falls in a period of weak Egyptian and Mesopotamian power, letting a Levantine kingdom control trade routes. He allied with Hiram of Tyre and married Pharaoh's daughter (1 Kgs 3:1), notable since Egyptian princesses were rarely given to foreign kings. The temple's plan (porch, hall, inner sanctuary) has close parallels in Syrian temples such as Ain Dara and Tell Tayinat.
28129: The temple shaped Israelite worship until 586 BC, and Solomon's prayer framed later Jewish prayer toward Jerusalem (Dan 6:10). His failures are blamed for the split of the kingdom (1 Kgs 11:11-13). Wisdom literature was gathered under his name, and later Jewish, Christian and Islamic tradition (Sulayman) made him the archetype of the wise king.
28130: Solomon wrote the Song of Songs in youth, Proverbs in maturity and Ecclesiastes in old age.
28131: Song of Songs Rabbah 1:1 (section number needs verification)
28132: Hezekiah and his colleagues wrote down (edited) Proverbs, the Song and Ecclesiastes.
28133: Solomon commanded demons through a ring given by God, used to build the temple.
28134: Testament of Solomon (pseudepigraphal, early centuries AD)
28135: The Ethiopian royal line descends from Menelik I, son of Solomon and the queen of Sheba.
28137: Eloquent and measured, fond of balanced sayings and observations about nature and human folly; in later life weary and reflective.
28150: Hearing of Solomon's fame, she comes with a great caravan of spices, gold and stones, tests him with hard questions, and blesses the LORD for setting him on the throne.
28151: Her kingdom, usually located in south-west Arabia (Yemen).
28154: An unnamed queen of Sheba, a kingdom usually located in south-west Arabia, travelled to Jerusalem to test Solomon's wisdom and exchange rich gifts, possibly also on trade business. Jesus cites her as a Gentile who came from the ends of the earth to hear wisdom and will condemn his unbelieving generation. Ethiopian and Islamic traditions developed extensive stories about her.
28155: Came to test Solomon with hard questions, was overwhelmed by his wisdom and court, praised the LORD, exchanged gifts and returned home (1 Kgs 10:1-13). Jesus calls her the queen of the south (Matt 12:42; Luke 11:31).
28157: Identified as Makeda, whose son by Solomon, Menelik I, founded the Solomonic dynasty and brought the ark to Aksum (Kebra Nagast).
28159: Sabaean inscriptions confirm a powerful incense-trading kingdom in Yemen, though its monarchy is attested mainly from the 8th century BC; some locate Sheba in north Arabia or link it with Ethiopia. No extra-biblical source names this queen.
28160: Her son Menelik I by Solomon founded Ethiopia's royal line.
28161: The Qur'an tells of a queen of Saba who comes to Solomon and submits to God; later commentators name her Bilqis.
28163: Regal, curious and testing; asks searching questions and is generous with praise once convinced.
28168: Rejects the elders' counsel at Shechem
28169: Asked to lighten Solomon's yoke, he follows his young advisers and promises scorpions instead of whips.
28171: Israel cries 'To your tents', stones his labour chief Adoram, and makes Jeroboam king.
28173: The prophet Shemaiah stops his campaign to reconquer Israel.

28175: Rehoboam, Solomon's son by Naamah the Ammonite, inherited a kingdom already strained by heavy labour and taxes. His harsh answer at Shechem triggered the secession of the ten northern tribes under Jeroboam, leaving him with Judah and Benjamin. His reign also saw religious decline and the invasion of Pharaoh Shishak, an event confirmed by Sheshonq I's relief at Karnak.

Listed in Jesus' genealogy (Matt 1:7).
28177: The Shechem episode is a classic lesson in servant leadership: the elders advise that if he serves the people they will serve him forever (1 Kgs 12:7). The text also sees God's hand fulfilling Ahijah's word (1 Kgs 12:15).
28178: The Karnak list of Sheshonq I names many towns in Israel and the Negev but, as preserved, not Jerusalem, prompting debate over whether Jerusalem paid tribute rather than being attacked.
28179: Brash and status-conscious, eager to prove himself tougher than his father; later chastened.
28181: The people contends, or may the people multiply
28184: first king of the northern kingdom
28189: The prophet Ahijah tears his cloak into twelve pieces and gives him ten; God promises him a lasting house if he obeys. Solomon seeks to kill him and he flees to Shishak in Egypt.
28191: Returning after Solomon's death, he is made king by the northern tribes and fortifies Shechem.
28192: Golden calves at Bethel and Dan
28193: Fearing pilgrimages to Jerusalem, he sets up two calves, appoints non-Levitical priests and a new feast in the eighth month.
28194: Rebuked by the man of God from Judah

28197: His disguised wife consults the blind Ahijah about their sick son, who dies as she enters Tirzah.

Kings measures nearly every later northern ruler by whether he walked in 'the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat'.

28202: Shrewd and capable, driven by political insecurity; justifies religious innovation as practical necessity.
28210: He marries the Sidonian princess and builds a temple and altar for Baal in Samaria.
28212: After three years of drought he meets Elijah ('troubler of Israel'), witnesses fire from heaven on Carmel, and rides to Jezreel ahead of the rain.
28214: Encouraged by prophets he defeats the Arameans twice, but spares Ben-hadad and is condemned for it.
28216: Jezebel has Naboth judicially murdered so Ahab can take his vineyard; Elijah pronounces doom, and Ahab's repentance delays it.

28219: Ahab son of Omri ruled the northern kingdom for twenty-two years and was, by Assyrian evidence, one of the strongest kings of his day. Kings judges him the most wicked Israelite king for promoting Baal worship with his wife Jezebel. His reign is the setting of Elijah's ministry, the contest on Mount Carmel and the murder of Naboth. He died in battle at Ramoth-gilead, as Micaiah had foretold.

28222: The Kurkh Monolith of Shalmaneser III lists 'Ahab the Israelite' contributing 2,000 chariots and 10,000 soldiers to the coalition at Qarqar in 853 BC. Scholars note the gap between his political strength and the biblical focus on his religious failure.
28223: Sulky, self-pitying and easily led, yet capable of bravado in war and of momentary contrition.
28231: Kills the prophets of the LORD
28232: She persecutes the LORD's prophets while supporting 450 prophets of Baal and 400 of Asherah at her table.
28234: After Carmel she vows to kill Elijah within a day, and he flees.
28236: Using letters in Ahab's name she arranges false witnesses and Naboth's stoning, so Ahab can take his vineyard.
28238: Painting her eyes and taunting Jehu from a window, she is thrown down by eunuchs and eaten by dogs, as Elijah foretold.
28239: Jezebel, daughter of Ethbaal king of Sidon, married Ahab and became the driving force behind Baal worship in Israel. She persecuted the LORD's prophets, threatened Elijah, and orchestrated the judicial murder of Naboth. She remained powerful as queen mother until Jehu's coup, when she was thrown from a window at Jezreel. In Revelation her name is applied to a false prophetess at Thyatira.
28240: Daughter of Ethbaal of the Sidonians (1 Kgs 16:31). Killed prophets of the LORD (1 Kgs 18:4), threatened Elijah (1 Kgs 19:2), plotted Naboth's death (1 Kgs 21). Incited Ahab to evil (1 Kgs 21:25). Died as Elijah foretold (2 Kgs 9:36). Name used for a teacher at Thyatira (Rev 2:20).
28242: Jezebel is the archetype of the idolatrous, manipulative ruler; her name became a byword.
